subject: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve NaN-scored candidate block indices (#57454)
pr_body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MegaAttention can fail startup with a DeepGEMM sparse-slot assertion during dummy prefill/autotuning. The candidate-source logits contain NaNs. Although `torch.topk` selects their block IDs, `value > -inf` discards them, leaving only the pinned newest block. Expanding that underfilled row repeats its last block inside the prefix DeepGEMM expects to be unique (389 copies of block 388 in the captured failing rows).

Exclude only the `-inf` padding sentinel when storing selected candidates. This retains NaN-scored block IDs, keeps the active prefix unique for the observed configuration, and works with the existing DeepGEMM dependency. Finite-score selection is unchanged; this adds no kernel, buffer, fallback, or host synchronization. It does not sanitize logits or fix the upstream numerical source of dummy-run NaNs.

Extend the existing candidate suite with empty/partial rows and aligned/unaligned starts under zero/NaN scores, and update its reference to retain selected NaN entries.

Validation on GB200:

- Both new NaN regression cases fail against the original selector; both finite control cases pass.
- All 13 candidate tests pass on PR commit `707b81b021`; scoped pre-commit hooks (including mypy) pass.
- Four captured TP-rank inputs replay through unmodified DeepGEMM after the fix, recovering 389 unique blocks in each previously failing row.
- Selector checks at 8K, 50K and 100K cover random, zero, NaN and mixed-NaN scores; finite outputs match the original exactly.
- The identical selector change on the previously validated model worktree passes real-weight TP4 MegaAttention startup with sparse logits, DSpark5, autotuning and FULL target/draft graphs. Short (18-token) and long (16,526-token) chat prompts both return the expected answer `4`. This is a serving smoke, not a full accuracy evaluation or a full-model build of current main. No full accuracy evaluation was repeated.

Duplicate-work check: #56558 optimizes the candidate-source selector but explicitly preserves NaN exclusion. #50201 and #49897 address the downstream token top-k kernel. None fixes this candidate-store predicate. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#16 instead adds repeate …[truncated]

subject: [NPU][bugfix] Fix NPU KernelLaunch Failure in rotate_input_ids_triton with Empty Batch (#30589)
pr_body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes an NPU runtime crash introduced by PR #28492 (Refactor / simplify MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner to use rotation).
When extend_seq_lens has a batch size of 0 (e.g., a DP rank with no active requests), rotate_input_ids_triton launches a triton kernel with an empty grid. This violates NPU parameter verification rules and triggers the error:

> KernelLaunch failed because value 0 for parameter coreDim is invalid. Expected value: not equal to 0.

Root cause is confirmed via commit comparison: the issue does not exist on pre-PR commit bf231f01, and stably reproduces on merged commit 24bf8d91.

## Modifications

- Add an early return guard in rotate_input_ids_triton: when batch_size == 0, return input_ids directly without launching the kernel.
- This handles the empty batch edge case for DP ranks with no requests, and avoids invalid kernel launches on NPU platforms.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy impact. The fix only skips kernel execution for empty batches and does not alter behavior for valid inputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact. The added boundary check has negligible overhead and only takes effect on empty batch scenarios.

subject: [Bugfix][Attention] Guard sparse MLA masked MHA workspace (#50906)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Sparse MLA masked-MHA builds a bit-packed top-k mask whose size is approximately:

```text
num_prefills × round_up(max_query_len, tile_m) × ceil(max_key_len / 32)
    × sizeof(int32)
```

The existing workspace was fixed at 64 MiB, while the routing matrix allows a
single 32K prefill to enter masked-MHA. Such a request requires exactly 128 MiB.
Heterogeneous batches can require even more despite staying within
`max_num_batched_tokens`.

Attempting to reshape the fixed workspace for an oversized mask can cause a CUDA
runtime error. Because CUDA execution is asynchronous, the API may have already
returned HTTP 200 before the worker reports the failure.

This PR:

- increases the top-k mask workspace from 64 MiB to 128 MiB, allowing the
  supported single-request 32K boundary to continue using masked-MHA;
- computes whether the actual workspace can hold every required suffix/context
  mask for the current prefill batch;
- includes that capacity check in the masked-MHA routing decision;
- falls back to the existing sparse MQA path when the mask does not fit;
- preserves the existing global-mask/per-context-chunk optimization behavior.

The workspace allocation increases by 64 MiB on workers where sparse masked-MHA
is available. Oversized batches do not trigger additional allocation.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR was found that addresses this masked-MHA top-k mask overflow.

Commands checked:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "masked MHA workspace"

gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "topk mask workspace"

gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "sparse MLA workspace"
```

Related work is different in scope:

- #50791 sizes the FlashInfer sparse-MLA decode workspace for DCP LSE.
- #50668 adds FlashMLA grid/workspace guardrails.
- #50613 changes MLA chunked-context scheduling but does not guard this top-k
  mask allocation.

## Test Plan

Run the workspace sizing and adjacent chunk-splitting tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  -k 'masked_mha_ …[truncated]

subject: [diffusion] fix: keep fused qk-norm-rope out of dynamo tracing (#31849)
pr_body:
## Motivation

With `torch.compile` enabled (e.g. `performance_mode=speed`), every qwen-image request fails with HTTP 500:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.AsPythonConstantNotImplementedError: SymNodeVariable() is not a constant
```

`can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` is decorated with `@torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`, but the qwen call sites pass `head_dim=img_query.shape[-1]` / `rope_dim=cos_sin_cache.size(-1)`, which become SymInts under dynamo tracing; `assume_constant_result` cannot fold SymInt arguments (wrapping in `int()` does not help — dynamo keeps them symbolic).

## Modifications

- Gate the fused inplace qk-norm-rope path with `not torch.compiler.is_compiling()`. Under compile, the unfused path is traced and inductor fuses it on its own; the handwritten fused kernel remains active for eager.
- Pass the static `self.head_dim` at the two qwen-image call sites instead of a runtime shape.

## Test

On 2×H100 (Qwen-Image-2512, 1024x1024, 50 steps, ulysses=2, torch.compile on): requests return 500 before this change and 200 after, with the compile path serving normally.

subject: [ROCm][LoRA] Fix MoE accuracy regression by preserving float32 router weight scaling (#31931)
pr_body:
Fixes MoE accuracy regression on ROCm introduced in #31676.

## Problem

PR #31676 reordered post-accumulation operations to add bias after dequantization. However, this also moved `MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT` after the `.to(compute_type)` precision conversion, causing router weight multiplication to occur in bf16/fp16 instead of float32.

This precision loss causes different outputs on ROCm due to differences in mixed-precision handling between ROCm and CUDA Triton backends. The issue manifests as non-deterministic expert routing, particularly visible in LoRA mixed-adapter tests.

## Root Cause

**Before #31676 (correct):**
```python
accumulator = accumulator * moe_weight  # float32
accumulator = accumulator.to(compute_type)  # float32 to bf16
```

**After #31676 (broken on ROCm):**
```python
accumulator = accumulator.to(compute_type)  # float32 to bf16
accumulator = accumulator * moe_weight  # bf16 x float32
```

## Fix

Restore `MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT` before precision conversion while preserving the correct bias placement after dequantization:
```python
# Router weights in float32 (before conversion)
if MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT:
    accumulator = accumulator * moe_weight[:, None]

# Dequantization + precision conversion
accumulator = accumulator.to(compute_type)

# Bias after dequantization (unchanged from #31676)
if HAS_BIAS:
    accumulator = accumulator + bias
```

## Testing

Fixes CI regression from: #31676

subject: [Fix] Correct W4AFP8 DeepEP scaling and mode-specific dtypes (#33669)
pr_body:
## Motivation

W4AFP8 with DeepEP had two independent failures in the same normal/prefill path.

First, `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` called `deepep_post_reorder_triton_kernel` without the required `routed_scaling_factor`, causing the original first-request `TypeError` in #33660. The model forward applies routed scaling after the cross-rank DeepEP combine, so this rank-local reduction must receive the neutral value `1.0`; using the model factor here would scale twice.

After the first fix, the reporter reproduced a second failure on 4xH200: DeepEP `intranode.cu:926` reported `Unsupported type`. That line is the normal **combine** dtype switch, not an INT4-weight dispatch site; DeepEP only transports activations and its normal combine accepts BF16. The actual problem was SGLang's dtype selection:

- W4AFP8 normal/prefill requantizes BF16 activations with checkpoint static scales, so its DeepEP payload must remain BF16.
- W4AFP8 low-latency/decode consumes DeepEP FP8 activations together with per-token-group scales, so that payload must remain FP8.
- With `--deepep-mode auto`, the previous global default selected FP8 for both implementations. The normal W4AFP8 path discarded the returned FP8 scale; a zero-token expert rank then returned an FP8 tensor directly to DeepEP's BF16-only normal combine, producing the reported assertion. Globally forcing BF16 would fix prefill but break low-latency decode.

Fixes #33660.

## Modifications

- Pass neutral `routed_scaling_factor=1.0` to the W4AFP8 DeepEP-normal post-reorder kernel.
- Let each concrete DeepEP implementation resolve a mode-specific dispatcher dtype.
- Configure W4AFP8 as normal=`bf16`, low-latency=`fp8`, including `auto` mode and TBO wrappers through the existing dispatcher configuration propagation.
- Add explicit guards for invalid normal and low-latency payloads, avoiding silent scale loss.
- Add CPU regressions for the kernel argument, per-mode dtype resolution, zero-token normal behavior, and missing low-latency scales.

## Accuracy Tests

The original routed-scale regression was run in the H20 SGLang image and passed before this update. The issue reporter independently confirmed that it fixes the ori …[truncated]

subject: [ROCm] [BugFix] Fix Quark GLM-5.2 Checkpoint inference: indexer wk per-channel FP8 dequant + missing sparse-MLA metadata fields (#48886)
pr_body:
## Summary

This PR addresses two independent bugs blocking quark quantized GLM-5.2 checkpoints with Attn quantized to PTPC FP8 from running end-to-end on ROCm (MI355X / gfx950). 

### Per-channel FP8 scale for fused indexer `wk` (`deepseek_v2.py`):

`_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` dequantizes the FP8 indexer `wk` weight to BF16 at load time so it can be fused with `weights_proj`. However, it unconditionally reads `scale_inv.shape[1]`, assuming a 2-D block-wise scale. Checkpoints that store `wk` with a 1-D per-output-channel scale crash at load with:
```
IndexError: tuple index out of range
# deepseek_v2.py: block_size = weight_fp8.shape[1] // scale_inv.shape[1]
```

Fix Added: branch on `scale_inv.ndim`. For a 1-D scale, use `GroupShape(1, in_features)` (per-output-channel); the original 2-D block path is unchanged. 

### Missing sparse-MLA metadata fields on the ROCm aiter backend:

#47327 refactored the shared MLA forward (`mla_attention.py`) to read `num_decodes`, `num_prefills`, `num_decode_tokens`, and `prefill_max_seq_len` from attention metadata, and updated the FlashMLA / FlashAttn sparse backends accordingly. `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata` was not updated, so inference crashes during graph capture with

```
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'num_decodes'
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'prefill_max_seq_len'
```

The ROCm sparse impl only implements `forward_mqa` (no `forward_mha`), so the dense-MHA prefill path added by #47327 was not viable on ROCm.

Fix:
- Add the metadata fields; populate `num_decodes` / `num_prefills` / `num_decode_tokens` in `build()` via the existing `split_decodes_and_prefills` helper.
- Add a `supports_dense_mha_prefill: ClassVar[bool] = True` capability flag to the base `AttentionImplBase`, set `False` on  `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`. When a sparse impl declares no dense-MHA path, `mla_attention.py` sets `prefill_backend = None` up front, so the shared forward takes the MQA-only path (existing behavior prior to #47327). 

## Test plan / results

Tested on 4x MI355X GPUs

  --model_args 'pretrained=<GL …[truncated]

subject: [bugfix][NPU] Fix startup bug in olmoe 1b 7b (#31782)
pr_body:
## Motivation



Serving `OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct` on Ascend NPU crashes on the first forward pass:

```
File ".../srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py", line 88, in _init_routing
    active_num=num_tokens * top_k,
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'int' and 'NoneType'
```

`top_k` reaches `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` as `None`.

**Root cause:** The NPU MoE refactor (#25663) moved `top_k` from being derived at runtime — the old `fused_moe_method_npu.py` always took `top_k = topk_ids.shape[1]` / `topk_weights.shape[-1]` inside forward — to being read once at construction time from `moe_runner_config.top_k` (cached as `AscendTPDispatcher.top_k`). Models that do not pass `top_k` into `FusedMoE` (e.g. `olmoe.py`, currently the only MoE model in-tree that omits it) leave `moe_runner_config.top_k = None`, and that `None` propagates through `AscendTPDispatcher.top_k` into `_init_routing`, blowing up at `num_tokens * top_k`.


## Modifications



- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/ascend_tp.py`: In `AscendTPDispatcher.dispatch()`, re-derive `self.top_k` from the actual topk output shape (`self.top_k = topk_weights.shape[-1]`) right before invoking `self.init._init_routing`.

This restores the pre-refactor protection where the routing kernel always used the runtime topk width, making the dispatcher robust to a `None` config `top_k` regardless of whether the model layer supplied it to `FusedMoE`. Single-file, minimal, no new compute (the topk tensor is already materialized in `dispatch()`).

## Accuracy Tests



NA

## Speed Tests and Profiling



N/A — correctness fix only. The change reassigns a scalar from a tensor shape that is already materialized in `dispatch()`; no new kernel calls or compute are introduced.

subject: [TPU][Bugfix] fix the MoE OOM issue (#20339)
pr_body:
## Purpose

The XLA backend for TPUs handles its own functionalization, so we don't need to wrap it as a custom operation to benefit from torch.compile's auto-functionalization. Additionally, using a custom operation would cause HBM OOM errors on TPU.

subject: [AMD][DSV4] fix: skip compressed-KV metadata on the draft worker in the HIP radix backend (#40205)
pr_body:
## Motivation


DeepSeek-V4 won't start on ROCm with any speculative algorithm. The draft worker dies during CUDA graph capture:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py", line 922,
    in make_forward_metadata_from_raw_verify
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py", line 620,
    in init_forward_metadata_indexer
  File "python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py", line 1833, in _indexer_pool
    assert pool is not None, (
AssertionError: No indexer pool for compression ratio 4
```
A draft pool has no ratio-4 layer. Its ratios get overwritten, the checkpoint isn't consulted (`kv_cache_configurator.py:1361-1372`):
```python
if self.is_draft_worker:
    compression_ratios = [COMPRESS_RATIO_NEXTN_LAYER] * self.layer_info.num_effective_layers
else:
    compression_ratios = self.model_config.compress_ratios
```

`COMPRESS_RATIO_NEXTN_LAYER` is 0. #38798 then started filtering `compressed_pool_configs` to the ratios a model actually has (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:948`), so the draft pool's `index_pools` is now empty, while three metadata builders in the HIP backend still pass `need_compress=True` unconditionally. Before that filter a ratio-4 indexer was always allocated and the draft worker found one it never used, which is why this went unnoticed.

Guarding the indexer alone isn't enough. The same builders then call `_attach_unified_kv_decode_streams`, which does
`csa_width=core.c4_sparse_page_indices.shape[1]` on a field that's `None` for the same reason, so the assert just becomes an `AttributeError`. That one only shows up under `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`; the assert happens either way.

Repro on `main` at `9784d5f979`, MI355X, ROCm 7.2. #40186 has to be applied first or startup dies earlier in pool sizing on an `UnboundLocalError`; it merged and current `main` already carries it.

## Modifications


One file, `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` (ROCm only).

`need_compress` is derived once in `__init__` instead of being hardcoded `True` at three call sites. `init_forward_metadata_target_verify_old` passes it down to `in …[truncated]

subject: elastic_ep: Fix issues with repeated scale up/down cycles (#37131)
pr_body:
This PR fixes two issues found when testing repeated scale up/down cycles:

1. PyNCCL communicators were never explicitly destroyed during
elastic EP reconfigurations. Over repeated scale up/down cycles,
this causes CUDA OOM crashes. Fixed by cleaning up PyNCCL correctly.

2. Elastic EP EPLB suppression was scattered across executor, worker, and
state-machine code, which made its lifecycle hard to follow and caused
bugs such as EPLB staying suppressed after scale down. Fixed by making
elastic_execute the sole owner of EPLB suppression.

While removing EPLB suppression from load_model, also clean up the
entire Elastic EP new-worker load path which was extremely messy:
Move EEP-specific logic from GPUWorker.load_model() into
elastic_execute, go through the same executor load path for both
regular and EEP new workers, and move the remaining scale-up logic,
such as receive_weights, into the elastic state machine where it belongs
(symmetric to existing-worker send_weights)

subject: [Bugfix][ROCM] Fix the MXFP8 block scale exponent (#53110)
pr_body:
The test belongs to the Kernels Root Misc Test group, which AMD CI does not run yet.
This fix should land before the PR that enables that group (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519).

## Purpose

The fused Triton MXFP8 quantizer picks the shared block scale with
`floor(log2(amax)) + 127`, which maps the block maximum onto 1.0 instead of onto
the top of the e4m3 range. Small elements of a block then land in the subnormal
region, so the Triton result drifts from `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch`, which
scales by `ceil(log2(amax / FP8_MAX))`.

`mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` only routes to the Triton kernel on ROCm, for the 2D
non-swizzled activation-quant case used by the native MX linear/MoE path, so the
mismatch does not appear on CUDA.

This change uses the same exponent as the torch reference and passes the e4m3
limit and the empty-block clamp in as constexprs, so both paths read off the same
`torch.finfo` values instead of hardcoding them.

## Test Plan

`tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py` exercises the Triton path against the
torch reference. The file is skipped outside ROCm.

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py
```

## Test Result

Without the fix the quantization cases fail the closeness check with
`assert 8 <= 1`. With the fix, on MI355 (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3):

```
55 passed, 17 warnings in 25.13s
```


---

subject: [DSA] Fix top-k v2 emitting invalid indices under tie overflow / inf scores (IMA in FA3 sparse decode) (#30645)
pr_body:
(generated by claude)

## Motivation

The nightly `test_glm52_fp8.py` perf test crashed with an illegal memory access on all three variants ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28986113304/job/86015497076)). The CUDA coredump shows the faulting kernel is **FA3 sparse decode** (`FlashAttnFwdSm90`, bs=1 decode right after an 8192-token prefill), and the faulting `LDGSTS` address is exactly `kv_pool_base - 1152B` (= one 576-elem bf16 DSA KV row) — i.e. FA3 dereferenced **KV slot index `-1`**.

The `-1` comes from the fused top-k v2 kernel. FA3 reads exactly `min(seq_len, topk)` entries of the top-k output (`dsa_cache_seqlens = seq_lens.clamp(max=topk)`), so every one of those slots must hold a valid index. Two data-dependent extremes break that contract:

1. **Tie overflow**: the collect pass keeps at most `kMaxNumTie = 1024` candidates from the threshold bin. When the bin holds more (ReLU-degenerate indexer scores easily put thousands of positions on one exact value — the random-token perf workload hits this; short gsm8k requests never reach the sparse path, which is why accuracy passed) and `topk - above_count > 1024`, `handle_tie` pads the remaining slots with `-1`. Unit repro on H200: seq=8320, topk=2048, 100 winners + 8220 zeros → **924 invalid entries inside the valid prefix**.
2. **inf / >65504 scores**: `coarse_bin_lower_bound` computed NaN boundaries for bins touching the fp16 ±inf keys (their neighbors live in NaN key space), so the collect pass matched nothing; large-but-finite scores (>65504, which fp16-round into the inf bin) were dropped entirely.

## Modifications

All in `topk_impl.cuh` (used by the v2 JIT kernel only; v1 is self-contained):

- **`kMaxNumTie` 1024 → 2048 (= `kMaxTopK`)**, with a `static_assert` pinning the invariant. 1536-style middle values don't close the hole: `remain = topk - above` reaches `topk` itself whenever `above == 0` (all-equal / inf-heavy rows). The tie buffer is **overlaid with the coarse histogram** (dead once `find_threshold` publishes the bin; `TieHandleSmem` and `tie_values` stay side by side since they are live together), so per-block shared memory *shrinks* from ~24.9KB to ~18.9KB.

subject: [CI Failure] Fix backend selection for encoder-only models (#28534)
pr_body:
## Purpose

After #24794, encoder-only models (e.g., BERT) fail to initialize because the TRITON_ATTN backend is selected by default, but it doesn't support encoder self-attention, causing:
```
NotImplementedError: Encoder self-attention and encoder/decoder cross-attention are not implemented for TritonAttentionImpl

This PR implemented an opt-in approach for attention type support:

    - Modified `EncoderOnlyAttention` to pass `attn_type=AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY`

  3. Explicitly marked the 3 backends that support encoder-only models:
    - FlexAttention: Supports DECODER + ENCODER_ONLY
    - FlashAttention: Supports DECODER + ENCODER_ONLY
    - CPU/TorchSDPA: Supports all attention types

subject: [Fix] Support ENCODER_ONLY target-verify in the trtllm_mha backend (#32178)
pr_body:
Block-diffusion draft models (DFlash / DSpark) declare `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` on their layers: the draft block is trained with bidirectional intra-block attention, and backends like flashinfer honor it via `causal=False`. The trtllm_mha backend never reads `layer.attn_type` — its TARGET_VERIFY path always runs the trtllm-gen spec-decode kernel, which is causal inside the verify window, so the draft block silently loses bidirectionality (draft quality degrades; outputs stay correct since verify is lossless, which is why no accuracy test catches it).

This PR routes ENCODER_ONLY layers through the plain decode kernel over `bs * L` single-token rows whose kv length spans the whole window (block K/V are written to the pool before attention, so every row attends prefix + the full block). Metadata expansion is gated to draft workers running DFLASH/DSPARK — target workers and other draft algorithms are untouched — and is recorded in the same body as the existing fused graph-metadata refresh, so eager and CUDA-graph paths stay consistent.

`test_trtllm_mha_encoder_only.py` pins both semantics against a paged SDPA reference: the spec-decode call is causal-in-window, and the expanded formulation matches the full-window (bidirectional) reference.

## Motivation


Inspired by @mickqian 

Diffusion FA backend was broken due to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16790/. 
The reason is `register_custom_op` (implemented in the torch.library.custom_op system) uses a Python function’s type annotations to generate a fixed op schema: the input types are fixed, and the number of return values is fixed as well.

In the code, the return type is annotated as Tuple[Tensor, Tensor], so the schema for this op becomes "it always returns two Tensors." We need to split it into two custom ops (one that returns only out, and another that returns (out, lse)), because a custom op’s number of return values can’t change dynamically based on a flag (the schema is fixed).
